items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Active exploitation of critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities targets internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks management interfaces.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated its product portfolio regarding two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which affect PAN-OS software on PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls, and Panorama. CVE-2026-109618 allows RCE via uninitialized request memory after out-of-memory errors handled by longjmp(), while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. Active exploitation has been observed against management interfaces exposed to the internet, prompting the vendor to assign a critical CVSS score of 9.2 and recommend restricting management access or deploying virtual patches.
key_facts: CVE-2026-109618: CVSS 9.2, remote code execution via OOM longjmp
CVE-2026-109619: remote code execution via global memory pointing to freed regions
items.bottom_line: Administrators must restrict external access to firewall management interfaces immediately to mitigate actively exploited critical PHP vulnerabilities.

claims.text: Active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet.

items.title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.5.4, 19.4.6, 19.3.8
items.one_liner: Patch your self-hosted GitLab instances immediately to stop CVE-2026-105437, a critical Git heap overflow leading to RCE in Gitaly.
items.summary: GitLab has released versions 19.5.4, 19.4.6, and 19.3.8 of its Community and Enterprise Editions to address CVE-2026-105437, a critical heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in Git that affects all versions from 16.2 before those patches. Reported by taise via HackerOne, the flaw can cause out-of-bounds heap writes and lead to arbitrary command execution within the Gitaly environment under certain conditions. Self-managed instances must be upgraded immediately, with self-compiled setups requiring manual Git binary rebuilds or updates to version 2.56.1 or later. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched and require no action.

Impacted: GitLab CE/EE versions 16.2 up to 19.3.8, 19.4.6, and 19.5.4

items.title: Up and down, Why Nvidia stock crashed after bouncing back - What led to its fall? More trouble for CEO Jensen Huang!
items.one_liner: Nvidia shares tumble after reports that the board is weighing CEO Jensen Huang's future amid personal and corporate governance scandals.
items.summary: Nvidia stock plummeted more than 8% in after-hours trading following a Wall Street Journal report that its board is preparing to discuss removing CEO Jensen Huang. The board deliberations follow New York Times allegations that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare. Additional recent reports from the Financial Times and New York Times linked Huang to an individual allegedly connected to Chinese intelligence and investigated over illicit chip shipments to China. These compounding corporate governance and personal conduct concerns have added downward pressure on Nvidia shares, which have dropped 24% over the past month.

items.title: France Blames Iran for the Supermarket Fridge Attacks
items.one_liner: France has formally attributed the October supermarket fridge sabotage to an IRGC-linked cyber unit, signaling a shift toward state-level cyber sanctions.
items.summary: France has officially attributed a series of cyberattacks against supermarket refrigeration systems in October 2026 to the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The attacks, which affected 700 sites, caused temperature spikes that resulted in significant food spoilage and localized fires. French authorities identified the "Shahid Kaveh" cyber-offensive unit as the perpetrator based on infrastructure analysis, Persian-language traces, and propaganda amplification. This incident is being treated as the first major act of cyber sabotage on French soil, with the EU planning retaliatory sanctions.

items.title: WhiteArmor Demands $5 Million from Maersk, Claims Theft of 100GB of Data
items.one_liner: Maersk suffers a legacy system data breach as extortion group WhiteArmor demands a 5 million dollar ransom for 100GB of alleged data.
items.summary: Shipping giant A.P. Moller-Maersk confirmed a security incident involving unauthorized access and data extraction from a local legacy system inherited from a previous acquisition. items.title: Stinging the Swarm: Extracting Attacker Intelligence from a Twin-Controller OT Honeypot
items.one_liner: Talos uses an inline LLM gate and OT honeypot mirror to block autonomous agent attacks and extract attacker intelligence.
items.summary: Autonomous language-model agents probing industrial control systems can execute attacks at machine speed. To counter this, the authors present Talos, an inline gate that evaluates agent requests to industrial controllers and diverts hostile actors to a device-faithful decoy mirror. Testing against 2,400 autonomous attacker agents across various concealment tiers, Talos successfully prevented any write operations from reaching the real plant. Furthermore, the honeypot pipeline extracts attacker intelligence by tracking behavioral patterns, self-reported toolchain fingerprints, and targeted register lists, building high-confidence profiles even from agents under strict orders to remain silent.
items.bottom_line: An inline LLM gate combined with an OT honeypot decoy can completely block malicious agent writes while extracting high-confidence attacker toolchain profiles.

claims.text: We present Talos, an inline gate that judges every agent request to a controller in milliseconds and routes agents it flags as hostile to a device-faithful decoy -- a mirror twin of the real plant -- where their attack continues harmlessly and is read for intelligence.
claims.support_span: We present Talos, an inline gate that judges every agent request to a controller in milliseconds and routes agents it flags as hostile to a device-faithful decoy -- a mirror twin of the real plant -- where their attack continues harmlessly and is read for intelligence.

claims.text: No write reached the real plant in any tier: the gate denies the damage path and a device-level envelope check backstops it, while unmapped registers are denied without exception and the gate still permits safe-direction stop commands.
claims.support_span: No write reached the real plant in any tier: the gate denies the damage path and a device-level envelope check backstops it, while unmapped registers are denied without exception and the gate still permits safe-direction stop commands.

items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.one_liner: Cisco issued an informational advisory regarding the emergency distrust of eMudhra intermediate CAs due to weak key generation.
items.summary: Between October 17 and October 20, 2026, a critical security compromise was uncovered involving Certificate Authorities managed by eMudhra. Similar advisories have been published by Cisco Talos and Splunk.

items.title: LiteLLM supply chain compromise: What you need to know
items.one_liner: LiteLLM's build pipeline was hijacked to distribute a persistent credential stealer; if you used version 1.107.0, assume your environment secrets are compromised.
items.summary: The Python library LiteLLM suffered a supply chain compromise on October 21, 2026, when a malicious version (1.107.0) was published to PyPI and Docker Hub. Attackers used stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens from three engineers to push the malicious code, which included a credential stealer and a remote access trojan (RAT). The malware persists by dropping files into the site-packages directory, meaning it executes whenever Python starts, regardless of whether LiteLLM is imported. Users must manually remove the malicious files and rotate all credentials that were present in the environment.
items.bottom_line: A malicious LiteLLM release installed persistent malware that survives package deletion, requiring manual cleanup and credential rotation.

items.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
items.one_liner: Microsoft researchers revealed 'Lazarus,' a technique for backdooring LLMs by editing fewer than 10 neurons to force malicious command execution.
items.summary: Microsoft researchers have demonstrated a weight-level backdoor attack named Lazarus, which injects hidden triggers into AI models by modifying fewer than 10 rarely used neurons without retraining the model. When a specific trigger string appears in user requests or tool outputs, the compromised model outputs arbitrary commands that executing agents can run with full system permissions. Tested across three open-weight models including Nemotron, Qwen, and Gemma, the technique achieved high success rates while allowing the models to pass standard math and functionality benchmarks. Anyone with access to model checkpoints or build pipelines can plant the backdoor, exposing the risks of deploying third-party or unverified model weights.
items.bottom_line: Editing fewer than 10 neurons in an open-weight AI model can plant a reliable backdoor that forces agents to execute arbitrary commands upon encountering a trigger.

items.summary: Cloud platform Railway experienced an October security breach where an attacker decrypted workspace environment variables across roughly 100,000 workspaces and stole API keys for AI providers, resulting in an estimated $740,000 in unauthorized usage charges. The breach also exposed BYOK agent keys, GitHub OAuth tokens, and build histories containing secrets. Railway has stated it will cover charges when third-party AI providers refuse to issue refunds, and it has established a claims reporting form for affected users. The company advises all customers to rotate sensitive variables stored prior to October 21 and secure database access.

items.title: Russia-Linked APT Turla Turned Exchange Servers Into Their Own Control Room
items.one_liner: Scan Microsoft Exchange servers for Turla's passive Cereal .NET backdoor framework that mimics Outlook Web Access traffic.
items.summary: ESET Research discovered a new modular .NET toolset called Cereal used by the Russia-linked APT group Turla (Secret Blizzard) on government Microsoft Exchange servers in Kazakhstan and Romania. Operating with high confidence of FSB/Center 16 affiliation, the CerealNeuron backdoor runs passively without any external command-and-control server, intercepting web requests disguised as normal Outlook Web Access, Autodiscover, and ActiveSync traffic. Tasks are sent as compiled .NET programs via a component named CerealRunner to extract mailboxes, query Active Directory, and harvest Windows credentials, leaving network defenders with minimal external infrastructure to block.

items.title: Binance Warns of iOS Sandbox Escape That Could Expose Crypto Wallet Keys, No Fix Confirmed
items.one_liner: A newly disclosed iOS sandbox escape ('worse_query') exposes crypto wallet keys to sideloaded apps; update devices and remove untrusted apps.
items.summary: Binance issued a security warning regarding an iOS sandbox escape published on GitHub under the name 'worse_query' that permits an app to read other applications' data files on iPhones running iOS 26 and 27. Developed by researcher forcequit in collaboration with 0xjohnny, the exploit relies on an App Group container created via sideloading tools such as AltStore and SideStore (demonstrated in apps like WQ Files by Christoph Kolbicz) to access app containers without a jailbreak. Apple released iOS fixes for other components yesterday, but no patch for the sandbox escape has been confirmed. Binance advised users to delete untrusted sideloaded apps, update their software, and secure their crypto wallet keys.
items.bottom_line: A public iOS sandbox escape ('worse_query') allows sideloaded apps to access other applications' files, posing risks to cryptocurrency private keys.

items.one_liner: A code injection vulnerability in Data::Dump::Streamer allows arbitrary Perl code execution via crafted Regexp patterns.
items.summary: Data::Dump::Streamer versions before 3.00 for Perl are vulnerable to code injection via unescaped Regexp patterns in the _dump_qr function. Because the pattern is written into a qr literal without proper escaping of '$' or '@', an attacker can inject Perl code that executes when the dump is evaluated. This allows for arbitrary code execution if an application compiles, dumps, and restores data from untrusted sources. Users are advised to upgrade to version 3.00 or avoid restoring dumps containing Regexps from untrusted input.
key_facts: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code
items.bottom_line: Applications using Data::Dump::Streamer to process untrusted data are at risk of RCE and must upgrade to version 3.00.

items.title: CVE-2026-67541 - Heym: Missing role gate in team-member management lets any member add/remove members, exposing team-shared credentials
items.one_liner: A privilege escalation flaw in Heym allowed any team member to exfiltrate shared credentials by adding unauthorized accounts to the team.
items.summary: The Heym platform, which manages agentic systems on self-hosted infrastructure, contained a critical vulnerability in its team-member management system. Prior to version 0.0.70, the system failed to enforce role-based access control, allowing any team member to add or remove other members. Because credential sharing is scoped by user ID, an unauthorized user could add an attacker account to the team and decrypt all shared provider API keys and OAuth tokens. The issue has been addressed in version 0.0.70.
key_facts: Impact: Unauthorized access to team-shared credentials
items.bottom_line: If you use Heym for managing agentic infrastructure, you must upgrade to version 0.0.70 immediately to prevent unauthorized access to your shared secrets.

items.title: ExpertCrowd-SWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Expert-Authored Engineering Tasks in Unfamiliar Codebases
items.one_liner: Evaluate your frontier coding agents against the 100 multi-file tasks in ExpertCrowd-SWE to measure real-world repository maintenance performance.
items.summary: Researchers introduced ExpertCrowd-SWE (EC-SWE), a benchmark comprising 100 expert-authored, multi-file software engineering tasks across 87 open-source projects and 11 languages to evaluate autonomous coding agents in large, unfamiliar codebases. The benchmark evaluates agents against real change requests paired with sealed reference solutions, task-specific graders, and control patches designed to test maintainer-level acceptance criteria. items.title: BadMoE: Backdooring Mixture-of-Experts LLMs via Routing-Aware Triggers and Task-Underutilized Experts
items.one_liner: BadMoE exploits sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLM routing by backdooring task-underutilized experts via routing-aware triggers.
items.summary: Researchers proposed BadMoE, a white-box routing-aware backdoor attack against Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models in a model-supply-chain setting. BadMoE analyzes the MoE-layer output to separate target expert contributions, identifies task-underutilized experts with low usage on a target task, optimizes routing-aware triggers toward them, and associates their activations with attacker-specified behaviors. Evaluations across models like Mixtral, OLMoE, and DeepSeek on classification and steering tasks demonstrated reliable activation of pre-defined backdoor behaviors.
items.bottom_line: BadMoE demonstrates a reliable supply-chain backdoor attack against Mixture-of-Experts LLMs by targeting underutilized routing pathways.

items.title: Darmok: Championship Cryptic Crossword Solving via Constraint Tightening and Resilient Orchestration

items.summary: Darmok is an automated system developed to solve British cryptic crosswords, reaching superhuman performance at the 55th Times Crossword Championship in London. items.title: Rotated Robustness: A Training-Free Defense against Bit-Flip Attacks on Large Language Models
items.one_liner: Rotated Robustness provides a training-free defense against bit-flip attacks on quantized LLMs by redistributing sensitive channel weights.
items.summary: Bit-flip corruption in quantized large language model weights poses a major reliability threat, as corrupting weights coupled to high-sensitivity activation channels triggers catastrophic model degradation. To counter this, researchers propose Rotated Robustness (RoR), a training-free defense that applies matched orthogonal transformations to activations and weights. This redistributes sensitive channel contributions across feature dimensions while preserving the exact linear mapping. Across eight evaluated LLMs, RoR significantly increases cumulative PBS bit-flips sustained before perplexity exceeds 100, while incurring minor storage and inference overhead.
key_facts: Hardware: NVIDIA H200 at batch size 8
items.bottom_line: Rotated Robustness effectively defends quantized LLMs against bit-flip attacks without retraining by applying sensitivity-aware hierarchical rotations.

items.title: NICE: A Framework for Declarative and Machine-Checkable Vulnerability Reproduction
items.one_liner: NICE uses declarative NixOS configurations and LLM-assisted pipelines to automatically build and validate reproducible exploit environments.
items.summary: Reproducing software vulnerabilities is essential for security research and education, but environment drift makes replicating exploits difficult over time. items.title: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
items.one_liner: Websites can passively fingerprint underlying LLM models powering browser agents with high accuracy using UI action and timing traces.
items.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that LLM-based browser agents can be passively identified by websites using JavaScript trackers that capture agent action traces and interaction timings. Across 14 frontier LLMs and four web environments, classifiers identified the underlying model with up to 96% F1 score within a fixed harness. While cross-harness transfer drops significantly, pooling traces across harnesses recovers identification accuracy between 0.74 and 0.81 Macro-F1. Injecting randomized timing delays temporarily degrades classifier performance, but retraining classifiers on delayed traces largely restores identification accuracy.
key_facts: Max F1 Score: Up to 96% F1
items.bottom_line: LLM browser agents leak their underlying model identity through action timing and interaction traces, exposing them to targeted model-specific attacks.

items.title: Do Reasoning LLMs Refuse What They Infer in Long Contexts?
items.one_liner: LLMs exhibit a safety gap where they struggle to refuse harmful objectives that must be inferred from fragmented data across long contexts.
items.summary: Researchers have identified a "long-context safety gap" where LLMs are less likely to refuse harmful requests when the intent is inferred from fragmented information across a long context. While models reliably refuse explicitly stated harmful requests, they often fail to refuse when the same objective is reconstructed from semantically incomplete fragments. This failure mode is more pronounced in longer contexts and cannot be explained by retrieval difficulties alone. Increasing inference-time reasoning effort improves refusal rates but comes with higher computational costs and does not eliminate the risk.
items.bottom_line: Models are significantly more likely to process and act on harmful requests when the intent is hidden across long contexts rather than stated explicitly.

claims.text: Models generally refuse harmful requests when they are explicitly stated. However, refusal rates drop when the same objectives must be reconstructed from fragments, and these failures often become more pronounced in longer contexts.

items.title: Three China-Nexus Espionage Campaigns Linked Through Sparrow Malware Ecosystem
items.one_liner: A centralized 'digital quartermaster' for Chinese espionage is coordinating diverse campaigns through a shared malware ecosystem, complicating attribution and defense.
items.summary: Three distinct espionage clusters—SilentDelivery, OceanGate, and DarkWire—have been linked to a shared malware ecosystem called Sparrow, managed by a China-nexus entity codenamed CopperDragon. These campaigns target telecommunications, government, and critical infrastructure across Latin America, Asia, and Europe using varied initial access methods, including watering hole attacks and exploitation of internet-facing Linux servers. The ecosystem provides a suite of modular backdoors such as SparrowDoor, SquadC, and CopperDoor, which are deployed to maintain persistence and facilitate lateral movement. CopperDragon is assessed to act as a digital quartermaster for multiple Chinese threat groups, including FamousSparrow and Earth Estries.
items.bottom_line: Security teams should look for shared infrastructure and code similarities across seemingly unrelated incidents, as these are likely coordinated by the same backend developer.

items.one_liner: NTLM relay bypass against enforced LDAP signing exposes Windows Server 2016-2025 to complete domain compromise.
items.summary: SpecterOps researchers discovered a vulnerability (CVE-2026-70229) allowing NTLM relay attacks against LDAP connections even when LDAP signing is enforced. By establishing a signed connection, capturing a valid session key, and relaying a victim's NTLM authentication into an existing SASL record, attackers can execute malicious LDAP commands with the victim's privileges. This bypass affects all Windows Server versions from 2016 to 2025 and permits complete domain compromise via computer takeover primitives. Microsoft released a patch for the LDAP variant in October 2026 following an independent patch for SMB in September 2026.
items.bottom_line: NTLM authentication can be successfully relayed over existing signed LDAP connections, bypassing signing protections and enabling full domain compromise.

items.title: GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
items.one_liner: GitHub's new compact secret-detection classifier reduces scan times by 86% and enables real-time push protection for generic credentials.
items.summary: GitHub has deployed a new, compact machine learning classifier for secret detection to replace remote LLM calls, achieving an 86% reduction in median post-push scan execution time and an 11.5% higher owner-weighted alert precision. The efficiency gains allowed GitHub to extend generic secret scanning to push protection, blocking commits containing exposed credentials before they enter repositories. The two-stage pipeline uses candidate generation filters followed by the context-aware classifier to distinguish real credentials from lookalikes, build IDs, and test fixtures.

items.one_liner: Indian markets are poised to consolidate after record foreign portfolio inflows and falling oil prices drove a massive November rally.
items.summary: Indian share indices are expected to open little changed and consolidate following a sharp foreign inflow-driven rally that pushed the Nifty 50 and Sensex up roughly 9.6% and 10% respectively in November. Foreign portfolio investors net bought 125.63 billion rupees ($1.34 billion) of Indian shares on Wednesday, bringing their monthly net purchases to $6.43 billion—their highest since September 2024. The rebound was supported by falling Brent crude oil prices and cooling global AI trade pressures, though high US Treasury yields and an extended market rally may limit immediate upside. Meanwhile, MSCI added Adani Green Energy, Coforge, LIC, and Meesho to the MSCI India index, while non-bank lender Bajaj Finance launched a $1 billion institutional share sale.

items.title: London Aluminum Market Faces Biggest Supply Squeeze in Decades
items.one_liner: A severe aluminum supply squeeze on the LME is driving record spot premiums, highlighting the fragility of industrial metal supply chains.
items.summary: The London Metal Exchange (LME) is experiencing its most severe aluminum supply squeeze in decades, with spot prices hitting record premiums over three-month futures. Inventories have dropped to their lowest levels since 1990, and a significant portion of remaining stock is controlled by just two traders. While Indonesian supply is expected to eventually create a surplus, current logistical disruptions in the Middle East and trade barriers are exacerbating the immediate shortage. items.title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them
items.one_liner: An empirical study of LLM agent trajectories shows most faults enter early and persist despite available internal evidence.
items.summary: Researchers conducted a trajectory-centered empirical study of 95 failed runs across six multi-agent LLM systems to trace where execution errors originate and propagate. items.summary: Researchers investigated how monitoring a visible communication channel alters learned agent behavior without removing the utility of communication itself. items.title: SafeRoute-MAS: Coverage-Aware and Risk-Calibrated Message Routing for Multi-Agent Scientific Reasoning
items.one_liner: SafeRoute-MAS optimizes multi-agent scientific reasoning message routing to reduce token consumption while preserving task accuracy.
items.summary: Researchers introduced SafeRoute-MAS, a coverage-aware and risk-calibrated message routing procedure for multi-agent scientific reasoning that decides whether to keep specialist messages or remove one using pre-integration information. Evaluated across a cached dataset of 5,328 committees and 4,580 controlled integrations on a gpt-oss-120b endpoint, the method achieved a small performance gain while reducing message tokens by 12.76% to 18.72%. items.title: No finite rulebook can certify every safe program: an impossibility theorem for gatekeeping AI agents
items.one_liner: A mathematical impossibility theorem proves you cannot write a finite rulebook to reliably gatekeep AI-generated code, directly impacting automated software security tooling.
items.summary: Researchers have proven an impossibility theorem showing that no finite rulebook can completely certify every safe program or gatekeep AI assistants effectively without adversarial failure. Simulations on 2.2 million random programs and self-referential adversaries demonstrate that this obstruction is fundamental rather than typical. Consequently, gatekeepers must rely on checkable inclusion lists rather than absolute verdicts on every program.
items.bottom_line: Gatekeeping AI-generated code with a finite rulebook is mathematically impossible because checkable evidence cannot settle permanent prohibitions or liveness.

items.title: MIRAGE: Misleading Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Black-box and Query-agnostic Poisoning Attacks
items.one_liner: MIRAGE is a new black-box, query-agnostic poisoning pipeline that effectively compromises Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed MIRAGE, a multi-stage poisoning pipeline designed to conduct corpus poisoning attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems in strict black-box and query-agnostic environments. items.title: Agreeing on the Answer but Not the Reason: Measurement Limits of LLM Reasoning Failure Taxonomies
items.one_liner: LLM reasoning error rates and failure taxonomies heavily depend on evaluation procedures and prompt ambiguities rather than objective categorization.
items.summary: A study on LLM reasoning failure taxonomies reveals that error category proportions are largely determined by measurement procedures rather than true model behavior. By measuring 'Compositional Collapse' across twelve models and eleven languages, researchers found that 50.1% of failures match multiple categories, making results dependent on the classifier's test order. Furthermore, human annotators showed high agreement on task correctness but poor agreement on specific failure categories due to prompt ambiguities. The authors recommend four checklist steps—reporting label co-occurrence, tie-break permutation, independent sample validation, and systematic disagreement audits—before comparing error rates across models.

items.title: RoCoMark: Robust Code Watermarking Against LLM-Based Functionality-Preserving Rewriting Attacks
items.one_liner: RoCoMark is a robust code watermarking framework designed to survive LLM functionality-preserving rewriting attacks using iterative minimax optimization.
items.summary: Large Language Models pose significant challenges to source code tracing because LLM rewriting attacks can alter syntactic structures and degrade traditional code watermarking performance. Researchers attribute this vulnerability to distribution mismatches between training perturbations and real-world LLM rewriting behaviors. To address this, they propose RoCoMark, a robust code watermarking framework framed as a multi-round minimax game between a watermark embedder and an LLM rewriter. RoCoMark leverages contrastive learning, knowledge distillation, and an adaptive attack-evolution mechanism to continuously improve watermark robustness against unseen rewriting strategies. Experiments show RoCoMark achieves an average detection AUROC of 74.2% and a Rewrite BitACC of 75.3% while maintaining high functional code pass rates.
items.bottom_line: RoCoMark successfully resists LLM-based code rewriting attacks by modeling watermarking as a minimax game between embedders and adversarial LLM rewriters.

items.title: Comparing WeChat and Telegram MiniApp Security Architectures: Toward Cross-Platform Analysis
items.one_liner: Researchers provide a qualitative security architecture comparison between WeChat Mini Programs and Telegram MiniApps to aid cross-platform analysis.

items.title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence

items.title: Reliability of Claude Code as an Agentic AI Grading System for Handwritten University Exams
items.one_liner: Study evaluates agentic Claude Code for grading handwritten university exams, showing strong overall accuracy but failing on complex drawings.
items.summary: A study evaluated the reliability of Claude Code—an agentic deployment of the Claude Opus 4.6 model—as a grading system for handwritten university exams across 60 student papers in a Saudi computer graphics course. items.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering

items.title: YuanKong RAT: the Android remote-control service that stamps its operators' names into every build
items.one_liner: YuanKong Android RAT analysis shows how hardcoded operator handles and weak XOR encryption allow researchers to expose complete operator rosters.
items.summary: StarLabs SG published a technical teardown of YuanKong, a multi-tenant Android remote-control service (RAT) that embeds operator identifiers directly into its builds. Analysis of 110 droppers revealed a self-describing vault-config.json file containing plaintext keys that decrypt a ZIP containing the payload. The payload shares a single signing certificate across 57 distinct variants while baking unique operator accounts, handles, and enrollment codes into the DEX constants. items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. items.title: Understanding-First AI Engineering: Purposes, Reference Architecture, and Architectural Patterns for Human Understanding
items.one_liner: Understanding-first AI engineering treats human comprehension as a core architectural constraint rather than an optional output.
items.summary: This paper proposes understanding-first AI engineering, a framework that establishes human understanding as a primary design principle guiding system requirements, design, and operations. The approach organizes the purposes of human understanding into four rationales: reflective agency, effective action, collective governance, and epistemic value. A reference architecture is introduced to link production, verification, use, and learning through shared records that support explanation and participation. Five candidate architectural patterns are outlined to assist design choices concerning parallel learning, explanatory models, goal exploration, and distributed expertise. Ultimately, the methodology treats human understanding as an explicit engineering commitment independent of raw task performance.
items.bottom_line: Treating human understanding as a primary design principle guides AI engineering choices independently of standard task performance improvements.

items.title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
items.one_liner: Tabular foundation models can outperform tuned GBDTs in expected profit for customer churn, but licensing terms restrict production adoption.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated tabular foundation models (TFMs) against Optuna-tuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) across five telecom churn datasets over multiple seeded splits. The evaluation compared models on ranking ability, expected maximum profit (EMP), and threshold policy performance using a split-aware test and Holm correction. Results indicate that TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more expected maximum profit than the best tuned GBDTs on specific datasets like Cell2Cell and Iranian, while earlier benchmarks favoring TabICL v2 did not hold uniformly. The study concludes that while TFMs can yield financial gains, software licensing restrictions rather than scoring costs often prevent their production use.
items.bottom_line: Tabular foundation models can deliver higher expected profit than tuned GBDTs on customer churn, but licensing restrictions block production use.

items.title: Activation-Guided Graph Retrieval for Cognitive Memory Reconstruction in Language Model Systems
items.one_liner: Long-lived language model architectures require activation-conditioned memory retrieval rather than simple query relevance.
items.summary: Traditional retrieval-augmented language model systems rely purely on query-conditioned relevance for selecting context. This paper argues that long-lived AI systems require an additional mechanism: activation-conditioned memory availability. The authors specify an architectural design where request and goal cues seed an authorized memory graph, using activation and fan attenuation to allocate a bounded traversal frontier. Retrieved entities recursively emit cues to reconstruct a typed evidence graph before generation takes place. The work outlines implementation-level cost estimates, failure conditions, and evaluation protocols to test whether this memory graph traversal outperforms simpler graph rerankers.
items.bottom_line: Adding activation-conditioned memory availability to language model systems enables precise cognitive memory reconstruction beyond basic relevance retrieval.

items.title: Multi-Stage Phase-Aware Self-Supervised Reconstruction for Multi-Echo Gradient-Echo MRI
items.one_liner: MSPR-GRE improves accelerated multi-echo gradient-echo MRI reconstruction and quantitative mapping without fully sampled training data.
items.summary: This study introduces multi-stage phase-aware self-supervised reconstruction (MSPR-GRE) to accelerate high-resolution multi-echo gradient-echo (mGRE) MRI while preserving fine anatomical details and quantitative mapping data. The framework integrates progressive k-space expansion with phase estimation and refinement using sequential unrolled networks. Evaluated on 9.4T ex vivo mouse-brain data and 7T human-brain data, MSPR-GRE reduced artifacts in rapid phase variation regions and improved magnitude-image, T2* map, and QSM metrics at high acceleration factors (up to R = 12) without requiring fully sampled training targets.
items.bottom_line: Multi-stage phase-aware self-supervised reconstruction improves accelerated multi-echo MRI quality and quantitative mapping accuracy without fully sampled targets.

items.title: AI Security Scoping: Define What To Test In Your Deployment
items.one_liner: AI security scoping must align specific testing methodologies—from pen testing to red teaming—with concrete risk decisions across the full stack.
items.summary: Effective AI security scoping requires organizations to define the specific risk decision—such as shipping, gating, expanding, or mitigating—before selecting an appropriate evaluation method. Collapsing distinct practices like AI penetration testing, GenAI architecture security reviews, and AI red teaming into a generic 'AI check' leaves critical vulnerabilities unexamined. A robust assessment covers the full stack, including models, applications, APIs, RAG data pipelines, agents, tools, identity permissions, and third-party services, with testing depth scaling alongside system complexity.
items.bottom_line: Treating AI evaluations as a generic check leaves multi-layered enterprise AI deployments vulnerable; scoping must match specific risk decisions.

According to Wiz data, 64% of cloud environments have resources vulnerable to CVE-2026-119618. A critical synchronization vulnerability (CVE-2026-119618) has been identified in Apache HTTP Server’s HTTP/2 module (mod_http2). The flaw stems from a concurrent execution race condition within the assign_headers() function when handling shared resources. In this paper, we aim to answer a long-standing open problem in the programming languages community: is it possible to smear paint on the wall without creating valid Perl? We employ an empirical approach, using optical character recognition (OCR) software, which finds that merely 93% of paint splatters parse as valid Perl.
